## Overview

This project uses a **clean architecture** approach where domain models are completely independent of the backend. You can swap Appwrite for Firebase, Supabase, or a REST API without changing your core models.

## Architecture Layers

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│         UI Layer (Widgets)          │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│    Repository Interfaces (Abstract) │  ← Backend agnostic
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│         Domain Models (Pure)        │  ← No backend deps
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Repository Implementations         │  ← Appwrite specific
│  (appwrite/, firebase/, etc.)       │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Directory Structure

```
lib/
├── models/
│   └── project.dart              # Pure domain models (no backend code)
│
├── repositories/
│   ├── board_repository.dart     # Abstract interface
│   ├── project_repository.dart   # Abstract interface
│   ├── user_repository.dart      # Abstract interface
│   │
│   └── appwrite/                 # Appwrite implementations
│       ├── appwrite_board_repository.dart
│       ├── appwrite_project_repository.dart
│       ├── appwrite_user_repository.dart
│       └── appwrite_config.dart
│
└── (your UI code here)
```

## Key Benefits

### ✅ Backend Independence
- Models have ZERO Appwrite imports
- Easy to switch backends later
- Can mock repositories for testing

### ✅ No Circular Dependencies
- Models use IDs instead of nested objects
- Clean serialization/deserialization
- No infinite loops

### ✅ Null Safety
- All `fromJson` methods handle null values
- Type-safe conversions
- Defensive parsing

### ✅ Appwrite Compatible
- Handles `$id` from Appwrite documents
- Works with Appwrite's query system
- Proper date/time handling

## Usage Examples

### 1. Initialize Appwrite (in main.dart)

```dart
import 'repositories/appwrite/appwrite_config.dart';

void main() {
  // Initialize Appwrite
  AppwriteConfig.init();

  runApp(MyApp());
}
```

### 2. Use Repositories in Your Widgets

```dart
import 'models/project.dart';
import 'repositories/appwrite/appwrite_config.dart';

class BoardScreen extends StatefulWidget {
  @override
  _BoardScreenState createState() => _BoardScreenState();
}

class _BoardScreenState extends State<BoardScreen> {
  final _boardRepo = AppwriteConfig.createBoardRepository();
  List<Card> cards = [];

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _loadCards();
  }

  Future<void> _loadCards() async {
    final loadedCards = await _boardRepo.getCardsByColumn('column123');
    setState(() {
      cards = loadedCards;
    });
  }

  Future<void> _createCard() async {
    final newCard = Card(
      id: '',  // Appwrite will generate
      columnId: 'column123',
      title: 'New Task',
      position: cards.length,
      assigneeIds: [],
      labelIds: [],
      priority: Priority.medium,
      createdAt: DateTime.now(),
      updatedAt: DateTime.now(),
      createdBy: 'user123',
    );

    final created = await _boardRepo.createCard(newCard);
    setState(() {
      cards.add(created);
    });
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    // Your UI code
  }
}
```

### 3. Move Cards Between Columns

```dart
Future<void> moveCard(Card card, String newColumnId) async {
  await _boardRepo.moveCard(card.id, newColumnId, 0);

  // Update local state
  setState(() {
    final updatedCard = card.copyWith(columnId: newColumnId);
    // Update your local list
  });
}
```

### 4. Update Card with copyWith

```dart
Future<void> updateCardTitle(Card card, String newTitle) async {
  final updated = card.copyWith(
    title: newTitle,
    updatedAt: DateTime.now(),
  );

  await _boardRepo.updateCard(updated);
}
```

## Appwrite Database Setup

### Collections to Create in Appwrite Console:

1. **projects**
   - Attributes: name (string), description (string), member_ids (array)

2. **boards**
   - Attributes: project_id (string), name (string), description (string), column_ids (array)

3. **columns**
   - Attributes: board_id (string), name (string), position (int), color (string), wip_limit (int), card_ids (array)

4. **cards**
   - Attributes: column_id (string), title (string), description (string), position (int), assignee_ids (array), label_ids (array), priority (string), due_date (datetime), comment_count (int), created_by (string)

5. **labels**
   - Attributes: board_id (string), name (string), color (string)

6. **comments**
   - Attributes: card_id (string), user_id (string), content (string)

7. **checklists**
   - Attributes: card_id (string), title (string), items (json array)

8. **users**
   - Attributes: name (string), email (string), avatar_url (string)

### Indexes to Create:

- **boards**: index on `project_id`
- **columns**: index on `board_id`, index on `position`
- **cards**: index on `column_id`, index on `position`, index on `created_by`
- **labels**: index on `board_id`
- **comments**: index on `card_id`
- **checklists**: index on `card_id`

## Switching Backends

To switch from Appwrite to another backend:

1. Keep all models in `lib/models/` unchanged
2. Keep all repository interfaces unchanged
3. Create new implementations (e.g., `lib/repositories/firebase/`)
4. Update your initialization code

```dart
// Before (Appwrite)
final repo = AppwriteConfig.createBoardRepository();

// After (Firebase - hypothetical)
final repo = FirebaseConfig.createBoardRepository();
```

Your UI code stays exactly the same!

## Best Practices

### ✅ DO
- Use repository interfaces in your widgets
- Use `copyWith` to update models
- Handle errors from repository methods
- Use IDs to reference related objects

### ❌ DON'T
- Import Appwrite in your UI code
- Modify models directly (use copyWith)
- Store nested objects in models
- Assume backend calls will succeed

```dart
  // ... implement other methods
}
```

## Model Quality Checks ✅

All models are validated for:
- ✅ No circular dependencies
- ✅ Use IDs instead of nested objects
- ✅ Null-safe deserialization
- ✅ Immutable with final fields
- ✅ copyWith methods for updates
- ✅ String-based enum serialization
- ✅ Appwrite `$id` compatibility
- ✅ Backend-agnostic design
